deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page, and it is not in Riemann's hand. It is an editorial note in German, signed 'W.', by Heinrich Weber, the editor of Riemann's Gesammelte mathematische Werke (1876; 2nd ed. 1892). It is a draft of the footnote attached to Abhandlung XIX, 'Versuch einer allgemeinen Auffassung der Integration und Differentiation'. The pencil header 'Riemann 7' and the folio number '1' are later archival marks.

Content, translated:
- The manuscript of the paper bears the date 14 January 1847, so it comes from Riemann's student years.
- Riemann surely did not intend to publish it.
- The investigation rests on foundations whose tenability he would no longer have accepted in later years.
- A struck-out sentence adds: 'As evidence for this there is an oral remark of Riemann to Dedekind.'
- Nevertheless the work is characteristic of Riemann's development, and its results are remarkable enough to justify including it in the collection.
- A second struck-out passage reads: 'In the notation for derivatives I have allowed myself a small change, since the one Riemann used seemed less convenient for printing than the customary notation now in use.'

Mathematical context (mine, not on the page): Abhandlung XIX is Riemann's early treatment of differentiation and integration of arbitrary (non-integer) order. Its integral operator is essentially what is now called the Riemann–Liouville fractional integral, I^a f(x) = 1/Gamma(a) * integral_c^x (x-t)^(a-1) f(t) dt. The page itself contains no derivation to reconstruct or check.

results.what: Editorial dating and assessment (14 Jan 1847, student work, shaky foundations, retained for its results) of Riemann's paper on generalized integration and differentiation, i.e. fractional calculus.
results.modern_name: Riemann–Liouville fractional integral/derivative (context only; no mathematics on this page)
results.usually_credited_to: Liouville (1832–1837) and Riemann (1847, published posthumously 1876); Weber wrote this editorial note

deep.surprise_reason: This is Weber's editorial footnote for the Gesammelte Werke, essentially as printed in 1876, plus two struck-out sentences. One mentions an oral remark of Riemann to Dedekind; the other mentions Weber's change of derivative notation. These are minor archival details of editorial history, with no new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: Context only, not on the page: the Riemann–Liouville integral of order a of t^b is Gamma(b+1)/Gamma(a+b+1) * x^(a+b). The difference should simplify to 0.

transcription_corrections: The hand is Heinrich Weber's (signed 'W.'), not Riemann's; the page is an editorial note, not a Riemann manuscript.
Heading: 'Note unter dem Text zu Abhandlung XIX' is correct; 'Integr.' abbreviates 'Integration'.
First struck-out passage: read 'Zum Beleg dafür liegt eine mündliche Äußerung Riemanns gegen Dedekind vor.' The word 'vor' begins the next line and is also struck through.

Second struck-out passage, opened by the bracket '[': 'In der Bezeichnung der Derivirten ... habe ich mir eine kleine Änderung gestattet, da die von Riemann angewandte für den Druck weniger bequem erschien als die sonst gebräuchliche ... übliche Bezeichnung.' The word read as 'erlaubte' at the end of the first line is uncertain. The whole passage is deleted.
The pencil '1' in the right margin is a folio number, not part of the text.
